Mackerel: Steel-blue back with repeated dark wavy bars, narrow tail stalk, dorsal/ventral finlets and a complete forked tail are visible. Body is horizontal and head right; image fills most width and appears below the requested side margins. Paired-fin separation is not fully established.
Haddock: Dark round shoulder thumbprint above the near pectoral, strong black lateral line and three separate dorsal fins are visible. Brown-grey silver body, two anal fins and complete tail. Generous empty border; chin barbel visible, far paired-fin separation unresolved.

Sardine: Silver flank with large reflective scales, dark blue back, one small dorsal and a deeply forked tail are visible. Straight horizontal right-facing fish; side margins are narrower than requested and far paired-fin roots are not separately established.
Anchovy: Bright silver flank stripe, large forward eye and a long open mouth reaching behind the eye are visible. Complete forked tail and horizontal body. An extra small dorsal nub near the tail and weak snout overhang need identity review; framing is wider than the requested half-canvas specimen.
Mullet: Faint longitudinal dark stripes follow the silvery scale rows; blunt head, small mouth and two separated dorsal fins are visible. Complete forked tail, horizontal profile and clear surrounding margin. Far paired fins are not fully distinguished.
Tarpon: Large silver plate scales, upturned broad jaw and a long trailing dorsal filament are visible; forked tail complete and body right-facing. Small extra dorsal nub near the tail requires identity review. Framing remains wider than the half-canvas request.
Snapper: Red-brown stout body with a continuous spiny dorsal, sloping pointed snout and visible front canine teeth. Complete tail and generous border. Teeth are pronounced; far paired fins remain partly overlapped and require anatomy scoring.
Curlew: Very long smooth downcurved bill, densely streaked brown plumage and two separated long legs with two visible feet. Short barred tail is visible below the folded wing at left; wing tips extend above it and ownership still needs scoring. Entire bill and toes fit inside the canvas.
Snipe: Long straight dagger bill, high rear-set eye, bold cream stripes along crown/back and dark patterned plumage are visible. Two separate legs and feet; short patterned tail projects below folded wing. Entire bill/toes remain inside clear border; wing/tail ownership not inferred from this view.
Plover: Compact upright brown-and-white bird with a large round dark eye, short stubby bill and black chest/face bands. Small centred specimen with generous margins; toe inventory and far-wing visibility still need G1 review.

Avocet: Thin bill curves upward at the tip, black-and-white pied feather blocks and long blue-grey legs are visible. Two separate ground contacts and generous margins. Short white tail appears beneath the folded wing, but the tail root/far wing remain partly overlapped.
Coot: Sooty black rounded body, white bill/forehead shield and broad grey-green toe lobes are visible. Two separate feet and generous border. The shield looks prominently raised; the short tail partly merges with folded-wing tips, so tail/far-wing identity remains unresolved.
Moorhen: Red forehead shield and red yellow-tipped bill, a clear white flank streak, and white undertail flashes are visible. Two separate green leg/foot contacts. Rail: Brown streaked upperparts, barred flanks, long toes on two separated feet and a cocked short tail are visible. Bee: Amber-and-black abdominal bands, dense golden thorax fur, veined translucent wings and a pollen-loaded hind leg are visible. Two antennae and broad border. Wasp: Strong yellow-and-black abdominal bands, narrow waist, pointed abdomen, two antennae and veined wings are visible. Six leg endpoints can be distinguished but some upper chains overlap and feet are at different heights. Thorax has visible hairs; natural count/attachment must be scored rather than assumed from endpoints.
Dragonfly: Long blue-marked rod abdomen, huge compound eye and four net-veined wings held outward are visible. Full abdomen tip and wings remain inside the canvas.
Damselfly: Needle-thin segmented blue-green abdomen, closed net-veined wings above the back, prominent side eye and two short antennae are visible. Mayfly: Two long posterior filaments, upright net-veined wings and a segmented slightly upcurved abdomen are visible. Body/head face right. Feet are uneven; wings and filaments fit within the canvas.
Stonefly: Flat overlapping veined wings, segmented brown abdomen, two short stout cerci and two long antennae are visible. Six correct thoracic legs are not established.
Giant Water Bug: Flattened oval brown wing covers and two hooked raptorial forelegs are visible. Several walking-leg branches overlap; exact six-leg inventory is unresolved. Antennae are unusually long and the exposed piercing beak is prominent rather than tucked, so identity needs review. View is oblique rather than strict side profile; broad margin retained.
